text: Add the screened request-context feature family to the additive user/video-ID scorer.
rationale: Training-only temporal screening found request_context (tab, hour, weekday) was the sole positively recommended feature group: +0.00221 primary lift, full coverage, and positive lift on all four screened dates. The official experiment should isolate this family without changing model or loss. Downside risks: the lift is smaller than its daily primary standard deviation (0.00580), context can be temporally nonstationary, and the result may improve broad ordering without placing positives in the top five.
exact_ablation: Relative to seed 0, append train-fitted categorical encodings for tab, hour, and weekday as additive feature weights; retain the seed optimizer, BCE loss, ID features, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.004 if context resolves within-user candidate differences; require a non-negative observed movement.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.003, but it may be flat because the screening evidence reports primary rather than a demonstrated top-five effect.

text: Replace additive user/video ID weights with a latent user-video dot-product model.
rationale: The seed includes only additive user and video identities, which cannot represent personalized user-video affinity. Train-only IDs are measured available inputs, and a dot product is a direct, ranking-relevant personalization ablation. Downside risks: sparse entities can overfit, unseen user/video IDs collapse to unknown representations, and GAUC can rise while nDCG@5 declines if broad affinities misplace the few top positives.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed additive scorer with b + b_user + b_video + dot(user_embedding_32, video_embedding_32), using train-only vocabularies and explicit unknown buckets; retain pointwise BCE and all other training settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase by 0.002 to 0.008 on warm user-video pairs because the score can model user-specific item preference.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely change between -0.001 and +0.005; top-five benefit is plausible but uncertain under temporal pair shift and OOV traffic.

text: Replace additive ID scoring with a 16-dimensional factorization-machine interaction between user and video IDs.
rationale: A compact factorization-machine scorer is a lower-capacity interaction alternative to additive IDs and tests whether latent pair affinity is useful without a deep model. User and video IDs are known at scoring time and present in the screened base. Downside risks: it may be too low-rank to capture heterogeneous preferences, may memorize rare entities, and cold entities receive little benefit.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed linear additive model with a second-order factorization machine over exactly the existing user_id and video_id fields using embedding dimension 16; preserve BCE, data processing, and training schedule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.006 if low-rank user-video interactions improve within-user pair ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.000 to 0.004 if the learned interactions concentrate positives near rank five; otherwise remain flat.

text: Replace the additive ID scorer with an embedding-plus-MLP pointwise ranker using only user and video IDs.
rationale: This tests nonlinear transformation of the same legal identity inputs, rather than adding unvalidated metadata or historical aggregates. It is materially distinct from a pure dot-product model because the MLP can learn nonlinear combinations of the two embeddings. Downside risks: substantially greater capacity can overfit sparse IDs, training may be less stable than the seed, and no measured evidence establishes that nonlinear capacity is needed.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed scorer with train-only user/video embeddings concatenated into a two-layer MLP with one scalar logit; keep the input fields, BCE target, temporal split, and evaluation artifact unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected movement is -0.001 to +0.006; a gain requires nonlinear ID interactions to generalize beyond the additive model.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected movement is -0.002 to +0.004; top-rank performance may regress if extra capacity amplifies noisy rare-ID effects.

text: Use user-normalized pointwise BCE instead of row-averaged BCE for the unchanged additive-ID seed.
rationale: The official GAUC is within-user and positive-count weighted, whereas the seed's row-average BCE can be dominated by prolific users. Equalizing each training user's total loss mass is a single objective ablation that may better align optimization with within-user ordering. Downside risks: the training user grouping may not correspond to a contemporaneous slate, reduced weight for active users can hurt both metrics, and this does not explicitly optimize nDCG@5.
exact_ablation: Keep the seed model and features unchanged, but replace row-mean BCE with BCE weighted by the inverse number of training rows for each user, with counts computed only from the complete training split.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.000 to 0.004 if long-history users currently dominate gradients; otherwise it can be flat or slightly negative.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected movement is -0.002 to +0.002 because user-normalized pointwise BCE has no direct top-five emphasis.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with a within-user positive-negative logistic pairwise ranking loss.
rationale: GAUC directly rewards positive-negative ordering within users, so a group-local pairwise objective is a clean objective-only test against the pointwise seed. The official task explicitly evaluates candidate variation within users. Downside risks: users without both labels provide no pairwise gradient, pair enumeration may increase runtime, and optimizing all pairwise errors can improve GAUC without improving the top five.
exact_ablation: Keep the seed additive-ID scorer unchanged and replace BCE with a deterministic within-user logistic loss over all training positive-negative row pairs, using only training rows and no cross-user pairs.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.005 if direct pairwise supervision better aligns scores with within-user AUC.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected movement is -0.001 to +0.003 because uniform pair weighting does not preferentially correct top-five misorders.

text: Add an nDCG@5-swap-weighted pairwise term to the seed BCE objective.
rationale: The primary objective averages GAUC and nDCG@5, and no available screen demonstrates a top-five gain. A small nDCG@5-focused ranking term is therefore a targeted attempt to improve the missing metric while retaining BCE's broad supervision. Downside risks: training groups may not be coherent slates, sparse mixed-label groups can make gradients noisy, pairwise ranking operations are costly, and an excessive ranking weight can reduce GAUC.
exact_ablation: Keep the seed model and BCE loss, and add one group-local LambdaRank-style logistic pair term weighted by detached binary nDCG@5 swap delta, with a fixed conservative coefficient of 0.1; all inputs and splits remain unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected movement is -0.001 to +0.003 because top-five-focused gradients trade some broad-pair ordering for head ranking.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.005 if training groups contain enough mixed-label comparisons affecting the first five ranks.

text: Apply count-aware L2 regularization to user and video ID weights in the additive seed.
rationale: The seed's shared L2 penalty treats one-observation and frequent entities equally even though train-only ID frequency is available. Stronger shrinkage for rare IDs may reduce temporal overfit while retaining the simple architecture. Downside risks: excessive shrinkage can erase rare but real preference signal, cannot solve OOV entities, and likely produces only a small effect.
exact_ablation: Keep the seed additive architecture and BCE unchanged, but replace uniform ID-weight L2 with train-frequency-scaled L2 for user and video parameters, computed exclusively from training rows and clipped to a fixed 1x-to-10x multiplier range.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected movement is -0.001 to +0.003, with benefit only if rare-ID overfitting is material.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected movement is -0.001 to +0.002; shrinkage may improve robustness but can suppress tail-item top-five positives.

text: Recency-weight the seed BCE loss using only training impression dates.
rationale: The validation period immediately follows the training period, so a modest recency weighting tests whether late-training preferences transfer better under temporal drift while using no future information. Date is an available impression-time field. Downside risks: it discards useful older observations, can worsen sparse-user/item estimates, and no measured temporal-drift screen supports a particular weighting strength.
exact_ablation: Keep seed features and architecture unchanged, but multiply each training BCE row loss by an exponential decay based only on its distance from the final training date, using a fixed 7-day half-life and normalizing total weight.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected movement is -0.002 to +0.003; it improves only if late-train ordering is more representative of validation.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected movement is -0.002 to +0.003; head ranking can improve under drift or regress from reduced effective sample size.

text: Add only the tab-by-hour categorical interaction to the additive seed.
rationale: The full request-context screen is positive and stable across all four screened days. A tab-by-hour interaction is a narrower, interpretable test of whether time-of-day preference depends on the request surface, without introducing user profiles, metadata, outcomes, or histories. Downside risks: the full-group gain may come from weekday rather than this interaction, rare combinations can overfit, and the crossed feature may duplicate additive context effects if those are absent from the seed.
exact_ablation: Relative to seed 0, append exactly one train-fitted categorical feature formed by crossing tab with hour derived from hourmin; do not add standalone context features or alter model/loss settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.000 to 0.003 if tab-specific hourly preference changes within-user candidate ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.000 to 0.002 if the interaction separates top candidates; otherwise likely flat.

text: Add weekday as the sole request-context feature to the additive seed.
rationale: Weekday is an impression-time field within the only positively screened feature family and provides a minimal causal context test. This is intentionally narrower than the full context-family candidate and can reveal whether a low-cardinality temporal effect transfers. Downside risks: the evidence supports the three-field family rather than weekday alone, day effects may be weak over the short validation span, and a globally additive weekday effect may not materially reorder items for a user.
exact_ablation: Relative to seed 0, append only a train-fitted categorical weekday feature as one additive field; retain all seed model and training settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected movement is -0.001 to +0.002 because weekday alone may provide limited within-user discrimination.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected movement is -0.001 to +0.001; a measurable top-five improvement is uncertain.

text: Add tab as the sole request-context feature to the additive seed.
rationale: Tab is a fully covered, impression-time context field belonging to the only feature family with positive training-only temporal screening. This isolated ablation tests whether request surface changes the relative relevance of displayed videos. Downside risks: tab may mostly shift calibration rather than within-user order, its apparent contribution is not separately measured from hour and weekday, and behavior can shift when tab traffic mix changes.
exact_ablation: Relative to seed 0, append only a train-fitted categorical tab feature as one additive field; leave user/video IDs, BCE, optimizer, split handling, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected movement is -0.001 to +0.003 if tab captures candidate-specific relevance differences beyond user and video IDs.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected movement is -0.001 to +0.002; top-five gains are possible but unproven by the aggregate screening result.
